scope: California outer coast, the 19 sectors in catalog/coastal-sectors.json. Inventory and planning record only: no app code reads this file.

labels.MEASURED: Read directly from a provider file, provider metadata or a published SkipperCast feed, retrieved on 2026-11-07 (times in fetch_log).
labels.ESTIMATED: Computed or inferred here: distances, nearest sector, coverage percentages from a hand-entered coast line, values taken from catalog text or documentation without re-reading the product, flags inferred from station type.
labels.UNKNOWN: Not determinable from the repo or the small public fetches.

method.stations: Part A covers every station in catalog/station-locations.json (39) plus the two alternates reviewed and rejected in catalog/station-failover.json (46259, 46286). Variables for NDBC/CDIP stations: any non-missing value in the NDBC realtime2 file over its newest 48 h. CO-OPS: the mdapi sensors list; prediction-only stations report tides only. Currents flags come from NDBC activestations.xml.
method.last_good: catalog/feed-health.json holds feed-level age limits (conditions 3 h, data 36 h, sst-fronts 48 h), not per-station times. last_good_in_published_feeds is the newest sample_at / last_success_at for the station across the published region feeds (conditions and data branches) read on 2026-11-07.
method.gaps: A hand-entered outer-coast line of 62 headlands and harbors, densified every 2 km (750 points, about 1442 km). A coast point is covered for a variable when a station reporting it lies within 25 nmi (46.3 km). A gap stretch is a run of uncovered points inside one sector at least 4 km long. Pass 1 uses inventory stations only; pass 2 adds every active NDBC-listed station in the California box (NDBC, CDIP, CeNCOOS, SCCOOS, NERRS, CO-OPS relays), CO-OPS water-level stations and CO-OPS tide-prediction stations. Candidates are pass-2 stations that would cover part of a stretch. Distance alone is not comparable exposure: every candidate needs the exposure review used in catalog/station-failover.json before it serves a region.
